alerts.alert: Server Leaks Information via "X-Powered-By" HTTP Response Header Field(s)
alerts.name: Server Leaks Information via "X-Powered-By" HTTP Response Header Field(s)
alerts.desc: The web/application server discloses technology environment details via the X-Powered-By header: Next.js.
alerts.solution: Ensure that your web server and application framework disables the X-Powered-By header in production (e.g. set poweredByHeader: false in next.config.ts).

alerts.name: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Contains "unsafe-inline"
alerts.desc: The Content Security Policy allows inline scripts through "script-src 'unsafe-inline'", which may reduce effectiveness against Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).
alerts.solution: Consider moving to cryptographic nonce-based or hash-based script authorization for Next.js scripts if inline execution can be avoided.

alerts.alert: Backend Infrastructure Disclosed via "x-vercel-id" and "x-vercel-cache" Headers
alerts.name: Backend Infrastructure Disclosed via "x-vercel-id" and "x-vercel-cache" Headers
alerts.desc: The response headers disclose backend serverless region routing and cache identifiers (sin1::iad1::h6nr8-1789549326948-3f4079d3a9d7).
alerts.solution: Configure reverse proxy or edge rules to strip internal routing headers if complete infrastructure masking is desired.

alerts.alert: Weak TLS Protocol Versions (TLS 1.0 / TLS 1.1) Offered on Edge
alerts.name: Weak TLS Protocol Versions (TLS 1.0 / TLS 1.1) Offered on Edge
alerts.desc: The server or edge proxy accepts handshake connections using deprecated TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 cipher suites (ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-SHA). These versions are deprecated under RFC 8996 and fail PCI-DSS v3.2.1.
alerts.solution: In the Cloudflare Dashboard, navigate to SSL/TLS -> Edge Certificates -> Minimum TLS Version and set the minimum allowed version to TLS 1.2.
